ja: **しよう**か
en: Shall we do it?; する is the do-everything verb and glues onto nouns to turn them into verbs — 攻撃する is to attack; the 〜よう form here offers to act rather than asking for permission

ja: **いる**のか
en: So you're here?; いる is existence for people and animals only — objects and situations take ある; it also carries the 〜ている progressive so watch which job it is doing

ja: するしか**ない**
en: We have no choice but to do it; ない is the negative of ある — plain nonexistence; as a verb ending it negates instead (しない) so decide each time between there isn't and doesn't

ja: **言[い]う**な
en: Don't say that; 言う is putting words out — quoted speech is marked with 〜と言う; the bare 〜な prohibition is blunt and men in this show use it freely

ja: **ある**と言[い]うのか
en: You're telling me there is one?; ある is existence for things and situations and also possession — 金がある means I have money; living beings switch to いる

ja: **俺[おれ]**に言[い]え
en: Tell me; 俺 is rough masculine I — fine with friends or thrown at an enemy but crude in front of a superior; Rimuru keeps it after becoming a slime

ja: 言[い]う**事[こと]**はない
en: There is nothing to say; 事 is an abstract matter or fact rather than an object — the physical side is 物; after a verb it packages the whole action as a thing

ja: **何[なに]**を言[い]っている
en: What are you saying?; 何 is なに alone but becomes なん before だ and counters — 何だ 何人; this line accuses someone of nonsense and expects no answer

ja: **それ**は俺[おれ]がする
en: I'll do that one; それ is near the listener or just mentioned while これ is on my side; it is the natural way to point back at what the other person raised

ja: 何[なに]に**なる**んだ
en: What is it turning into?; なる is a change of state that happens to you and marks the result with に — 魔王になる; deliberate doing stays with する

ja: それで**いい**
en: That will do; いい is the spoken form of 良い and often means fine as is — 「いい」 alone can decline an offer so tone separates praise from refusal

ja: **この**俺[おれ]がする
en: I'll be the one to do it; この must sit in front of a noun and never stands alone like これ; この俺 is a boast meaning me of all people

ja: **私[わたし]**は何[なに]もしない
en: I'm not doing anything; 私 is the neutral first person anyone can use though men sound formal with it; 何も plus a negative means nothing at all

ja: **そう**言[い]う事[こと]か
en: So that's how it is?; そう means that way and points back at what was just said — alone it answers exactly; そういう in front of a noun means that sort of

ja: **その**事[こと]は私[わたし]がする
en: I'll handle that matter; その is the noun-attaching partner of それ; switch to それ when the thing needs no naming after it

ja: 俺[おれ]は**魔王[まおう]**だ
en: I am the demon lord; 魔王 is a rank in this world — the top tier of monster ruler and not the Christian devil; it decomposes into 魔 demonic plus 王 king

ja: **これ**は何[なに]だ
en: What is this?; これ is a thing in my own space and works as a noun so it takes は and を — この cannot do that and needs a noun behind it

ja: 俺[おれ]が**やる**
en: I'll do it; やる is blunt casual する and also means to give to someone beneath you; 「やってやる」 turns menacing so keep it out of polite speech

ja: **お前[まえ]**がやるのか
en: You're the one doing it?; お前 is rough second person — normal between fighting men or close friends and insulting to a stranger or a superior

ja: **どう**する
en: What do we do?; どう asks in what way or what state and fills out the こう そう ああ どう manner set; it cannot stand before a noun the way どの does

ja: 魔王[まおう]が**来[く]る**
en: The demon lord is coming; 来る is irregular — 来[き]ます 来[こ]ない 来[き]て; it means motion toward the speaker so answering a call is 行く not 来る

ja: これを**くれ**
en: Give me this; くれる is giving toward me or my side and never me handing something out; 〜てくれ is a rough request while 〜てくれない softens it

ja: 私[わたし]にも**できる**
en: I can do it too; できる is the potential of する so the thing you can do takes が not を; it also means to be finished or to come into existence

ja: そう**思[おも]った**
en: That's what I thought; 思う is a gut impression or opinion while 考える is reasoning something through; 〜と思う is how any claim gets softened into a personal view

ja: これはいい**物[もの]**だ
en: This is a good item; 物 is a physical object against abstract 事; alone it reads もの but compounds switch it to ぶつ as in 動物 and もつ as in 荷物

ja: 俺[おれ]も**行[い]く**
en: I'm going too; 行く is motion away from where the speaker stands — say 今行く to answer someone calling you; its past 行った is irregular

ja: 魔王[まおう]を**見[み]た**
en: I saw the demon lord; 見る is plain seeing or watching — 見せる is to show and 見える is what is visible without effort; 〜てみる after a verb means give it a try

ja: 魔王[まおう]になる**者[もの]**だ
en: He's the one who will become demon lord; 者 is a person defined by a role and lives in compounds like 勇者 and 王者; it sounds flat or cold so never apply it to yourself politely

ja: **我[われ]**は行[い]く
en: I shall go; 我 is archaic lofty I — dragons and demon lords use it to sound ancient; modern speech keeps it only in set forms like 我々

ja: お前[まえ]も**魔物[まもの]**か
en: So you're a monster too?; 魔物 is literally demon plus thing — any hostile magical creature; it names the species while 魔王 is a title one of them holds

ja: お前[まえ]の事[こと]は**分[わ]かって**いる
en: I know all about you; 分かる is understanding that arrives on its own so what is understood takes が; 知る is picking up a fact while 分かる is it becoming clear

ja: **あなた**も来[く]るか
en: Are you coming too?; あなた is polite but distancing and Japanese normally uses the person's name instead; a wife calling her husband あなた is the dear usage

ja: **今[いま]**行[い]く
en: I'm on my way; 今 is this moment — 今から from now and 今まで until now; 今行く sounds like coming in English because motion is judged from the speaker

ja: **ここ**にいるぞ
en: I'm right here; ここ そこ あそこ divide space by whose side it is on and ここ is mine; ここ also means at this point in a story or argument

ja: **誰[だれ]**が言[い]った
en: Who said that?; 誰 as the subject takes が and never は; 誰か is someone and 誰も with a negative is nobody

ja: ここで**待[ま]って**いる
en: I'll be waiting here; 待つ takes what you await with を; the bare 待って is a shout to freeze someone mid-action rather than a request for patience

ja: 待[ま]って**ください**
en: Please wait; ください is the polite form of くれる asking someone to act for your benefit; attach it to a 〜て form for normal politeness since plain 〜て stays casual

ja: 俺[おれ]は**スライム**になった
en: I became a slime; スライム is the bottom of this world's monster ranking which is the joke in the title; katakana marks it as a borrowing from game fantasy

ja: あなたはいい**方[かた]**だ
en: You are a good person; read かた it is a respectful word for a person while the same kanji read ほう means direction or side — both grow out of way

ja: この**国[くに]**の魔王[まおう]だ
en: He's the demon lord of this country; 国 is a country or realm and also one's home region; here it covers human kingdoms and monster territories alike

ja: **そんな**事[こと]はない
en: That's not true; そんな is that kind of and attaches straight to a noun as the な shape of the その set; そんな事はない denies what was just claimed

ja: **訳[わけ]**が分[わ]からない
en: It makes no sense; 訳 is the reason or logic behind something so 訳が分からない is bewilderment rather than not knowing a fact; 〜という訳だ closes off an explanation

ja: **奴[やつ]**は魔物[まもの]だ
en: That guy is a monster; 奴 carries contempt or rough affection and never goes to someone present who outranks you; あいつ is the everyday equivalent

ja: **もう**いい
en: That's enough; もう looks at a change that has already landed and flips to not any more with a negative; もういい cuts a conversation off in irritation

ja: **みんな**で行[い]こう
en: Let's all go; みんな is everyone taken as one group and 皆さん is the polite version; みんなで means as a group rather than together with everybody

ja: それを**もらう**ぞ
en: I'll be taking that; もらう is receiving from the other side and mirrors くれる with the receiver as subject; 〜てもらう means you got someone to act for you

ja: **ちょっと**待[ま]って
en: Hold on a moment; ちょっと means a bit but mostly softens what follows; left hanging with a pause it becomes a polite refusal rather than a small amount

ja: **話[はなし]**の分[わ]かる奴[やつ]だ
en: He's a reasonable guy; 話 is talk or a story treated as a thing you can hand around and the verb behind it is 話す; 話が分かる means someone gets it

ja: 私[わたし]の話[はなし]を**聞[き]け**
en: Listen to me; 聞く covers both listening and asking — 話を聞く listen and 道を聞く ask directions; sound that reaches you without effort is 聞こえる

ja: **本当[ほんとう]**の事[こと]を言[い]え
en: Tell me the truth; 本当 is literally real plus hitting the mark and turns into the adverb really as 本当に; 本当? on its own asks if someone is serious

ja: そんな**気[き]**がする
en: I have that kind of feeling; 気 is the catch-all word for mind and mood; 気がする is a hunch you cannot justify not a conclusion you reasoned out

ja: **まあ**いい
en: Well fine; まあ concedes ground before you speak; here it drops a complaint rather than agreeing

ja: **オーク**が来[き]た
en: The orcs are here; katakana for orc — in this show a pig-faced race whose starving horde drives the first war and whose leader takes the オークロード title; unrelated to the tree oak

ja: 俺[おれ]の**力[ちから]**を見[み]ろ
en: Witness my power; 力 spans muscle strength and political clout; as a suffix it reads りょく as in 魔力

ja: ここに**置[お]いて**くれ
en: Put it down here; 置く is setting an object down and leaving it; the 〜ておく form means doing something in advance

ja: お前[まえ]の**名[な]**は何[なん]だ
en: What is your name; bare 名 is terse and old-fashioned next to everyday 名前; monsters receiving a 名 from Rimuru is the show's central mechanic

ja: 俺[おれ]は何[なに]も**知[し]らない**
en: I know nothing; 知る is holding information while 分かる is grasping meaning; the present 知る often means to find out so the state is 知っている

ja: これが**我[わ]が**国[くに]だ
en: This is my country; 我が is grand written-style possession used by kings and generals; 我 reads わ here not われ

ja: **相手[あいて]**は魔王[まおう]だ
en: Our opponent is a demon lord; 相手 is whoever is facing you so it covers enemy partner and conversation partner alike

ja: その**時[とき]**が来[き]た
en: The moment has come; 時 as a noun is a point in time; after a verb it becomes the when clause and never means whereupon

ja: **魔法[まほう]**でやる
en: I will do it with magic; 魔法 is spellcraft as a discipline while 魔力 is the raw energy it burns

ja: いい**所[ところ]**だな
en: Nice place; 所 is a spot or location and also an abstract point as in that is where he is wrong

ja: **貴様[きさま]**に力[ちから]はない
en: You have no power; 貴様 is written with polite characters but is pure hostility now; shouting it picks a fight

ja: **先生[せんせい]**は魔法[まほう]を知[し]っている
en: The teacher knows magic; 先生 literally born earlier and is used for doctors and masters of a craft not only schoolteachers

ja: この国[くに]の**王[おう]**は誰[だれ]だ
en: Who is the king of this country; 王 is a rank word that mostly lives inside compounds like 魔王 and 王国

ja: **こっち**に来[こ]い
en: Come over here; こっち is the casual こちら; it also stands in for me and my side as in こっちの負け

ja: ちょっと**考[かんが]えさせて**くれ
en: Let me think for a second; 考える is deliberate reasoning you can be interrupted in unlike 思う which is an impression that just arrives

ja: その**人[ひと]**を知[し]っている
en: I know that person; 人 is a person as a human being; 者 is colder and slots into compounds like 勇者

ja: 本当[ほんとう]の事[こと]を言[い]って**しまった**
en: I went and told the truth; 〜てしまう marks an action as finished and usually regretted; casual speech contracts it to 〜ちゃった

ja: **前[まえ]**を見[み]ろ
en: Eyes front; 前 covers both in front of and earlier than; time and space share one word

ja: **後[あと]**で聞[き]く
en: I will ask later; 後 read あと means afterwards in time; the same kanji reads うし in 後ろ for physically behind

ja: ここで**死[し]ぬ**のか
en: So this is where I die; 死ぬ is blunt and plain; it is one of the few verbs conjugating on the ぬ pattern

ja: この**世界[せかい]**に来[き]た
en: I came to this world; 世界 is generation plus boundary; the isekai genre hangs on this one noun

ja: あなたが我[わ]が**主[あるじ]**か
en: Are you my master; 主 read あるじ is the lord you serve; the same kanji is しゅ in 主人 and ぬし in 持ち主

ja: これが**王国[おうこく]**の力[ちから]か
en: So this is the kingdom's strength; 王国 is king plus country; a 魔王 rules a 魔国 not a 王国

ja: 国[くに]を**作[つく]る**
en: I am going to build a country; 作る is making concrete things and organisations; 造る is for large-scale manufacture and 創る for creation from nothing

ja: この**町[まち]**に人[ひと]はいない
en: There is nobody in this town; 町 is a town or a city district; 村 is smaller and 市 is administrative

ja: お前[まえ]は**強[つよ]い**な
en: You are strong; 強い covers physical strength skill level and intensity of flavour or wind; it never means merely large

ja: 俺[おれ]たちは**人間[にんげん]**じゃない
en: We are not human; 人間 is humans as a species and is the line monsters are measured against; use 人 for a person you can point at

ja: 国[くに]の**ため**に死[し]ぬ
en: To die for one's country; ため is for the sake of after の and because of after a past verb; context alone separates purpose from cause

ja: **よく**分[わ]かった
en: Now I get it; よく is the adverb of いい and stretches to often and to a sarcastic how dare you as in よく言えるな

ja: **凄[すご]い**力[ちから]だ
en: What incredible power; 凄い originally meant ghastly and now praises; before an adjective it is spoken as すごく or casually すげえ

ja: **さすが**我[わ]が主[あるじ]だ
en: Just what I expect of my master; さすが is admiration for someone living up to their reputation; it is praise never surprise

ja: **そして**魔王[まおう]になった
en: And then he became a demon lord; そして chains events in sequence; それから stresses the gap in time and それで stresses the consequence

ja: この**手[て]**でやる
en: I'll do it with my own hands; 手 stretches from hand to move method and manpower as in 手を出す meaning to meddle

ja: **持[も]って**行[い]け
en: Take it with you; 持つ is holding in the hand and also possessing; 持って行く and 持って来る are how Japanese says take and bring

ja: この**スキル**は凄[すご]い
en: This skill is amazing; スキル in this show is a named system ability with fixed effects not a talent you practise into being

ja: **そこ**で待[ま]っていろ
en: Wait right there; そこ is near the listener; ここ is at me and あそこ is away from us both

ja: **じゃあ**どうする
en: So what do we do; じゃあ is spoken では and pivots off what was just said; it also softens a goodbye

ja: どうする**つもり**だ
en: What do you intend to do; つもり is your own plan or intention; claiming someone else's つもり sounds accusing

ja: ここは俺[おれ]に**任[まか]せろ**
en: Leave this to me; 任せる hands over both the work and the decisions; 預ける is only for physically leaving something in someone's care

ja: **あれ**が魔王[まおう]の国[くに]か
en: So that is the demon lord's country; あれ is far from speaker and listener alike; it also refers to a thing you both already know without naming it

ja: **精霊[せいれい]**を見[み]た
en: I saw a spirit; 精霊 are elemental beings tied to nature; 幽霊 is the ghost of a dead person

ja: お前[まえ]の言[い]う**通[とお]り**だ
en: You are exactly right; 通り as a noun is a street; after の or a verb it means just as and is read とおり

ja: 誰[だれ]かいる**みたい**だ
en: Sounds like somebody is here; みたい is casual spoken inference from what you sense; らしい leans on hearsay and ようだ is the formal version

ja: **こんな**所[ところ]で死[し]ぬのか
en: I die in a place like this; こんな describes a kind of thing near me and often carries contempt; この simply points

ja: **こう**やるんだ
en: You do it like this; こう is this manner and pairs with そう and ああ; use it while demonstrating

ja: お前[まえ]は俺[おれ]の**部下[ぶか]**だ
en: You are my subordinate; 部下 is section plus below so it is a chain-of-command word; a plain employee is 社員

ja: **しかし**相手[あいて]は魔王[まおう]だ
en: But our opponent is a demon lord; しかし is stiffer than でも and でも cannot start a written sentence as cleanly

ja: **やっぱり**お前[まえ]は強[つよ]い
en: You really are strong after all; やっぱり confirms a suspicion you already had; the formal form is やはり

ja: **こいつ**は強[つよ]い奴[やつ]だ
en: This guy is strong; こいつ is これ turned into a person — pointing at someone right beside you with the same bluntness you would use for an object; so it lands as either affection between rough friends or contempt for an enemy

ja: 手[て]を**出[だ]す**な
en: Keep your hands off; 出す is the transitive partner of 出る — you push something out; 手を出す means to meddle or start a fight rather than literally extend an arm

ja: **二人[ふたり]**で行[い]こう
en: Let's go the two of us; 人 is read り in the small counters ひとり and ふたり only — from three people on it is さんにん with にん

ja: **問題[もんだい]**は何[なに]だ
en: What's the problem; 問題 covers both a trouble and an exam question — the compound is ask + topic; so a maths problem and a political problem take the same word

ja: もう**大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]**だ
en: I'm fine now; 大丈夫 answers about safety and condition; on its own it also works as a polite refusal — someone offering you food hears no

ja: **ゴブリン**の町[まち]を作[つく]る
en: We'll build a goblin town; ゴブリン and the other monster races are katakana loans grafted onto this world's ranking system — the show treats them as a species name and a class of strength

ja: **出[で]る**時[とき]が来[き]た
en: The time to leave has come; 出る is intransitive — the subject itself emerges; so it covers leaving a place and a monster appearing — never taking a thing out

ja: その力[ちから]が**欲[ほ]しい**
en: I want that power; 欲しい is an adjective describing the thing wanted with が not を — for wanting to do an action you need 〜たい instead

ja: お前[まえ]は**馬鹿[ばか]**か
en: Are you an idiot; 馬鹿 is the standard insult but between allies it comes out as exasperated teasing — tone carries all the weight since the word itself is everyday

ja: **自分[じぶん]**で考[かんが]えろ
en: Think for yourself; 自分 reflects back to whoever the sentence is about — so it means myself here and yourself in a command; it is not a fixed first person pronoun

ja: 魔法[まほう]を**使[つか]う**
en: I'll use magic; 使う is to employ a tool or a person for a purpose — using up a resource or spending money needs a different verb

ja: 話[はなし]は**以上[いじょう]**だ
en: That's all I have to say; 以上 is "this and above" so it means at or over a number — at the end of a speech or list it signals nothing follows

ja: **君[きみ]**の名[な]を聞[き]きたい
en: I'd like to hear your name; 君 is warmer than お前 and used downward or between equals — a superior addressed as 君 would take it as presumptuous

ja: お前[まえ]に**頼[たの]む**
en: I'm counting on you; 頼む is asking a favour you trust the person to carry — it also orders food and as 頼むよ becomes a pleading please

ja: 力[ちから]を**見[み]せて**やる
en: I'll show you my power; 見せる is the causative-flavoured pair of 見る — you put something in view; unlike 教える which imparts information

ja: それは**可能[かのう]**か
en: Is that possible; 可能 states an objective possibility about a situation while できる conjugates as a verb about an actor's ability

ja: 俺[おれ]が**悪[わる]かった**
en: That was my fault; 悪い in the past tense is a casual apology among men; 悪いな is the everyday sorry — far lighter than the word bad suggests

ja: この**音[おと]**は何[なに]だ
en: What is this sound; 音 is any noise a thing makes while 声 is a voice from a living throat — a monster's roar can take either depending on framing

ja: その**男[おとこ]**は誰[だれ]だ
en: Who is that man; 男 is the plain biological label and calling someone あの男 keeps them at a cold distance — for a polite man you would say 人 or 方

ja: もう一[いち]**度[ど]**言[い]ってくれ
en: Say that once more; 度 counts occasions after a number so 一度 is once and 今度 is next time — the same kanji also counts degrees of temperature

ja: **まだ**分[わ]からない
en: I still don't know; まだ with a negative means not yet and leaves the door open — もう with a negative closes it and means not any more

ja: これで**全[すべ]て**だ
en: That's everything; 全て is a stiff written-feeling all that sums up items or facts — for people in a room みんな is the natural choice

ja: **必要[ひつよう]**な物[もの]を出[だ]せ
en: Hand over what's needed; 必要 marks something required by a situation rather than wanted by a person — pair it with が for what you need

ja: 話[はなし]を聞[き]かせて**いただく**
en: Allow me to hear your story; いただく is the humble もらう that lowers the speaker while raising the giver — いただきます before a meal is the same verb

ja: **今日[きょう]**はここまでだ
en: That's it for today; 今日 keeps its irregular reading きょう while the same kanji pair reads こんにち in greetings

ja: 時[とき]が**過[す]ぎた**
en: Time has passed; 過ぎる is something moving past a point on its own — attached to an adjective it means excessively so as in 強すぎる

ja: **少[すこ]し**強[つよ]くなった
en: I've gotten a little stronger; 少し is the neutral written-safe a little while ちょっと is its casual cousin that also softens requests and refusals

ja: 手[て]に**取[と]って**見[み]ろ
en: Pick it up and look; 取る is grabbing and removing with the hand — it stretches to taking a break or taking notes but never to photographing

ja: 名[な]を**付[つ]けて**やる
en: I'll give you a name; 付ける attaches one thing to another so it also switches lights on — naming works because the name sticks to the bearer

ja: **なるほど**そういう訳[わけ]か
en: I see so that's the reason; なるほど acknowledges that an explanation adds up and is not simple agreement — overusing it to a superior sounds like you are grading them

ja: **あいつ**は俺[おれ]の部下[ぶか]だ
en: That guy is my subordinate; あいつ is the あれ series so the person is away from both speakers — it is rough and often said behind their back

ja: この**子[こ]**は人間[にんげん]か
en: Is this child a human; 子 alone is a short affectionate word for a young one and この子 can even point at a pet or a small monster

ja: **わし**が相手[あいて]だ
en: I'll be your opponent; わし marks an old man's speech in fiction and instantly ages the speaker — a young character using it would sound like a joke

ja: もう**済[す]んだ**事[こと]だ
en: It's already settled; 済む is a matter reaching completion by itself with no actor named; 終わる just ends while 済む implies the business is discharged

ja: **子供[こども]**が二人[ふたり]いる
en: There are two children; 子供 is the full noun for a child in general and is also thrown at adults acting childish — 子 by itself is closer to my kid

ja: **森[もり]**に誰[だれ]かいる
en: Someone's in the forest; 森 is a dense wild wood where things live while 林 is a thinner stand of trees — the show's 森 is monster territory

ja: **風呂[ふろ]**を作[つく]ろう
en: Let's build a bath; 風呂 is the soaking tub and the bathing room itself; Rimuru builds one for the goblins because a real 風呂 is a communal comfort not just washing

ja: **早[はや]く**来[こ]い
en: Come quickly; 早い is early in time and by extension quick to happen — for high speed of motion the same reading is written 速い

ja: **竜[りゅう]**の力[ちから]をもらった
en: I received a dragon's power; 竜 is the eastern serpentine dragon of legend rather than the western winged lizard — in this world it is the top of the monster hierarchy

ja: 俺[おれ]を**呼[よ]んだ**か
en: Did you call me; 呼ぶ is calling out to summon someone and also naming — 〜と呼ぶ means to call something by that name

ja: この国[くに]を**守[まも]る**
en: I will protect this country; 守る is guarding something you value against harm and also keeping a promise or a rule — 助ける is rescuing after harm starts

ja: **あの**男[おとこ]は魔王[まおう]だ
en: That man is a demon lord; あの points at something distant from both of us or shared in memory — the drawn out あのー is a separate hesitation filler

ja: **殺[ころ]す**つもりはない
en: I don't intend to kill you; 殺す is the blunt transitive kill and 死ぬ is dying on one's own — mixing them up is the classic transitivity trap

ja: それは相手[あいて]に**よる**
en: That depends on the opponent; よる is almost always kana and appears as 〜による meaning depending on or caused by — a bare よる rarely stands alone

ja: 自分[じぶん]の**目[め]**で見[み]ろ
en: See it with your own eyes; 目 is the eye and also stretches to a viewpoint or attention — Rimuru is a slime with 魔狼の目 so the word carries his gained senses

ja: **勝[か]つ**のは我[われ]だ
en: The one who wins is me; 勝つ takes に for the party you beat not を as in 相手に勝つ; the opponent is what you prevail against

ja: **旦那[だんな]**は凄[すご]い人[ひと]だ
en: The boss is an amazing man; 旦那 is a merchant's friendly sir for a male customer or patron and separately a woman's word for her husband

ja: ここは**どこ**だ
en: Where is this place; どこ asks for a location and the isekai staple ここはどこだ literally asks what this place is — Japanese frames being lost as a where question

ja: 王[おう]が**なさった**事[こと]だ
en: It was the king who did it; なさる is the honorific する used about a superior's actions and never about your own — its imperative 〜なさい is what a parent barks

ja: 私[わたし]の考[かんが]えは**違[ちが]う**
en: My thinking is different; 違う is the everyday way to say that's wrong because being wrong is framed as differing from the fact — 間違う is the heavier make a mistake

ja: 俺[おれ]の**仲間[なかま]**だ
en: He's one of my comrades; 仲間 is anyone inside your circle — party member or fellow crew — not a personal friend in the 友達 sense

ja: **オーガ**が来[く]るぞ
en: The ogres are coming; katakana loanword kept distinct from オーク the orc — the show's ogres are the tall horned warriors who become Benimaru's people

ja: **まさか**あいつが魔王[まおう]か
en: No way — that guy is a demon lord?; まさか voices flat disbelief at something you just realized; it also stands alone as You can't be serious

ja: **一人[ひとり]**で行[い]く
en: I'll go alone; the counter 人 goes irregular here as ひとり; the word carries both one person and by oneself so context decides which

ja: **今回[こんかい]**は違[ちが]う
en: This time is different; 回 counts occurrences so 今回 frames one specific round or attempt — 今 alone is just the present moment

ja: 俺[おれ]が**戦[たたか]う**
en: I'll do the fighting; combat between two sides so the opponent is marked with と not を; 戦い is the noun

ja: **敵[てき]**は強[つよ]い
en: The enemy is strong; 敵 is the hostile side you must beat while 相手 is a neutral counterpart — a partner or opponent in a match

ja: もう**やめろ**
en: Cut it out already; やめる is dropping an action you were doing; the bare imperative やめろ is shouted and blunt

ja: 人間[にんげん]の**勇者[ゆうしゃ]**か
en: So you're the humans' hero; literally brave person but here it is a class — the champion granted power to kill demon lords rather than a compliment

ja: 力[ちから]を**得[え]た**
en: I have obtained power; える is stiff and bookish where spoken Japanese says 手に入れる; stuck on a verb stem 〜得る means can

ja: お前[まえ]を**認[みと]める**
en: I recognize you; 認める is conceding a fact or granting someone standing; 認められる is the moment the group finally accepts you

ja: **確[たし]か**な話[はなし]か
en: Is that reliable information?; as a な-adjective it means solid and certain but dropped at the head of a sentence 確か flips to hedging — if I remember right

ja: その**まま**でいい
en: Leave it as it is; まま is a state held unchanged; そのまま means don't touch it and 〜たまま means while still doing

ja: 森[もり]の**中[なか]**だ
en: It's inside the forest; なか is the interior; the same kanji reads ちゅう in 集中 and じゅう in 世界中 meaning all over

ja: 町[まち]に**入[はい]る**
en: We're entering the town; intransitive so the place takes に; 入れる is putting a thing in and 風呂に入る is how you say taking a bath

ja: お前[まえ]を**許[ゆる]さない**
en: I won't forgive you; one verb for both pardoning and permitting; 許せない is the stock line for something unforgivable

ja: **他[ほか]**の者[もの]はいるか
en: Is there anyone else?; ほか is the remainder besides this one; 他に? on its own asks anything else while the same kanji reads た in 他人

ja: そんなの**嫌[いや]**だ
en: I don't want that; a な-adjective of distaste rather than a verb; barked alone いや is a flat refusal and far sharper than 好きじゃない

ja: **名前[なまえ]**は何[なん]だ
en: What's your name?; 名 plus 前; 名 lives in compounds while 名前 is the standalone word — and in this show bestowing a 名前 on a monster makes it stronger

ja: **年[とし]**を取[と]ったな
en: You've gotten old; read とし it covers both year and a person's age; 年を取る is the set phrase for aging and compounds shift to ねん

ja: 我[われ]ら**一同[いちどう]**の主[あるじ]だ
en: He is master to all of us; 一同 treats the gathered group as one formal body and normally trails the group name as in 家臣一同 where conversation would just say みんな

ja: **僕[ぼく]**が守[まも]る
en: I'll protect you; a soft masculine I used by boys and mild-mannered men; it sits between blunt 俺 and neutral 私

ja: **いつ**来[く]るんだ
en: When is he coming?; the question word when; いつも and いつか are built on it whereas 時 only marks a moment and cannot ask

ja: **進化[しんか]**したのか
en: You evolved?; 進 advance plus 化 change; here it is a monster ranking up into a new body and title — used for creatures never for gadgets

ja: 何[なに]も**見[み]えない**
en: I can't see a thing; 見える is something being in view on its own; deliberate looking is 見る and 見られる is the potential or passive

ja: 何[なに]を**食[く]った**
en: What did you eat?; rough masculine eating next to neutral 食べる; it also shows up in idioms like 時間を食う meaning to eat up time

ja: **姿[すがた]**が違[ちが]う
en: Your form is different; 姿 is the whole visible figure or silhouette rather than a face; 姿を消す is to vanish

ja: **もし**死[し]んだらどうする
en: What if you die?; もし flags a hypothetical before it arrives and pairs with 〜たら or 〜ば; the conditional works without it so もし is just early warning

ja: その話[はなし]は**面白[おもしろ]い**
en: That story is interesting; it stretches from funny to intriguing; 楽しい is the fun you feel yourself while 面白い is a property of the thing

ja: 俺[おれ]を**信[しん]じろ**
en: Trust me; one verb for trusting a person and believing a claim; 信じられない is the everyday I can't believe it

ja: そう**願[ねが]う**よ
en: I certainly hope so; 願う is wishing or petitioning; the frozen お願いします is the same verb worn down into the all-purpose please while 頼む is a direct ask of someone

ja: 魔法[まほう]を**かける**
en: I'll cast a spell; a single verb covering hanging pouring and phoning; with 魔法 it becomes casting and it usually stays in kana

ja: 俺[おれ]の魔法[まほう]を**受[う]けろ**
en: Take my magic; 受ける is absorbing what comes at you — an attack a test a favor; もらう is about being handed something you wanted

ja: 早[はや]く**帰[かえ]ろう**
en: Let's head home soon; 帰る means returning to where you belong so it implies home or base; the identical-sounding 変える is to change something

ja: この国[くに]を**支配[しはい]する**
en: I will rule this country; 支 hold up plus 配 distribute; it is domination over subjects not mere administration and 支配者 is the ruler

ja: 私[わたし]が**致[いた]します**
en: I shall do it; 致す is the humble する used looking up at a superior — how the retainers speak to Rimuru; どういたしまして is the same verb frozen

ja: この町[まち]が**好[す]き**だ
en: I love this town; a な-adjective so the thing liked is marked が never を; there is no verb to like and 大好き is the intensified form

ja: **暴風[ぼうふう]**の竜[りゅう]だ
en: It's the storm dragon; 暴 violent plus 風 wind; this is Veldora's title 暴風竜 rather than the ordinary word for bad weather which is 嵐

ja: あいつは**魔人[まじん]**か
en: Is that guy a demon-kin?; 魔 demon plus 人 person; a humanoid whose power ranks far above a plain 魔物 yet below the 魔王 rank

ja: **次[つぎ]**は俺[おれ]だ
en: I'm next; 次 is the following item in a sequence; 後 only means later in time so a queue takes 次

ja: お前[まえ]は**英雄[えいゆう]**だ
en: You are a hero; 英雄 is greatness earned through deeds and remembered by history while 勇者 is a class handed to a summoned champion

ja: 一人[ひとり]で**食[た]べる**
en: I'll eat by myself; the neutral everyday verb; 食う is coarse and いただく is the humble polite version at the table

ja: 勇者[ゆうしゃ]を**召喚[しょうかん]する**
en: They're summoning a hero; 召 summon plus 喚 cry out; a ritual dragging someone across worlds unlike 呼ぶ which is calling across a room

ja: 二人[ふたり]の**間[あいだ]**に入[はい]る
en: I'll step in between the two of them; あいだ is the span separating two points or people; the kanji turns into かん in 時間 and ま in 間違い

ja: 町[まち]に**戻[もど]る**
en: I'm going back to town; intransitive returning to an earlier spot with no sense of home; 戻す is putting an object back

ja: **協力[きょうりょく]**してくれ
en: Work with me on this; 協 join forces plus 力 strength; it is cooperation between equals and the partner is marked with と

ja: **吾輩[わがはい]**は竜[りゅう]である
en: I am a dragon; a pompous archaic I — Veldora's chosen pronoun; readers know it from the novel 吾輩は猫である so it sounds grandly out of date

ja: 敵[てき]が**動[うご]いた**
en: The enemy has moved; intransitive so people machines and plans all 動く by themselves; making something move is 動かす

ja: 魔王[まおう]を**倒[たお]す**
en: We'll bring down the demon lord; transitive knocking an opponent over hence defeating a boss; falling by yourself is 倒れる

ja: **もっと**力[ちから]が欲[ほ]しい
en: I want more power; もっと asks for a greater degree of the same thing; a different one is 他の

ja: そんな事[こと]は**ダメ**だ
en: You can't do that; ダメ is a flat refusal — the root sense is useless or broken — so it covers both no good and not allowed

ja: 魔王[まおう]が**復活[ふっかつ]**した
en: The demon lord has revived; 復活 is "again" + "live" — used for resurrection and also for anything revived like a scrapped plan

ja: **準備[じゅんび]**はできたか
en: Are you ready?; 準備 is the whole process of getting set up; 用意 points at laying out the actual items

ja: これが俺[おれ]の**仕事[しごと]**だ
en: This is my job; 仕事 is the work or duty itself — not the workplace and not employment status

ja: そんなに**簡単[かんたん]**じゃない
en: It isn't that easy; 簡単 spans simple in structure and easy to do; it takes な before a noun

ja: **心配[しんぱい]**するな
en: Don't worry; 心配 is anxiety about a specific person or outcome; 心配してくれる is how you thank someone for worrying

ja: **体[からだ]**が動[うご]かない
en: My body won't move; 体 includes physical condition and stamina; the bare torso sense is 身[み]

ja: その**剣[けん]**を見[み]せてくれ
en: Let me see that sword; 剣 is a straight double-edged blade — the curved Japanese sword is 刀

ja: 王国[おうこく]の**騎士[きし]**が来[き]た
en: The kingdom's knights are here; 騎士 is literally "riding retainer" — a titled human soldier class never used for monsters

ja: **用意[ようい]**はいいか
en: All set?; 用意 is having things laid out and to hand; 準備 is the broader getting-ready

ja: あの**エルフ**は強[つよ]い
en: That elf is strong; エルフ is the Western fantasy race; 妖精[ようせい] is a small fairy and not the same thing

ja: お前[まえ]は**悪魔[あくま]**か
en: Are you a devil?; 悪魔 is "evil" + "demon" for a malevolent spirit; 魔物 is any monster and 魔王 is a rank

ja: 敵[てき]が**攻撃[こうげき]**してきた
en: The enemy attacked; 攻撃 is a noun that becomes a verb with する; skill names in the show are built the same way

ja: もっと**頑張[がんば]れ**
en: Try harder!; 頑張る is sustained enduring effort rather than one burst; 頑張れ is the standard shout of encouragement

ja: 先生[せんせい]に**会[あ]いたい**
en: I want to see the teacher; 会う takes に not を and covers both a planned meeting and bumping into someone

ja: ここにある**はず**だ
en: It should be here; はず is confident inference from evidence — not obligation and weaker than certainty

ja: **約束[やくそく]**を守[まも]る
en: I keep my promises; 約束する is to promise while keeping one is 約束を守る and breaking it is 約束を破[やぶ]る

ja: これは**うまい**な
en: This is good; うまい is casual for tasty and also for skillful; 美味[おい]しい is politer and food only

ja: こいつが**首領[しゅりょう]**か
en: So this guy is the chief; 首領 heads a band or gang — heavier and more feared than リーダー

ja: あの男[おとこ]は**商人[しょうにん]**だ
en: That man is a merchant; 商人 is a trader by profession; a specific shop takes 〜屋[や] instead

ja: **情報[じょうほう]**が欲[ほ]しい
en: I want information; 情報 is gathered intelligence or news; stored knowledge is 知識[ちしき]

ja: **さて**次[つぎ]は何[なに]だ
en: Now then what's next; さて marks a shift to the next topic or task and carries no meaning inside the sentence

ja: **声[こえ]**を出[だ]すな
en: Don't make a sound; 声 is specifically sound from a living throat — every other noise is 音

ja: **もちろん**やるさ
en: Of course I'll do it; もちろん literally means needless to argue and asserts the obvious; it is not a polite yes

ja: **次回[じかい]**も見[み]てくれ
en: Watch next time too; 次回 counts the next installment of a series; plain 次 is next in any sequence

ja: みんなを**助[たす]けたい**
en: I want to save everyone; 助ける is rescue from real danger while everyday helping out is 手伝[てつだ]う

ja: **黒[くろ]**い目[め]をしている
en: It has black eyes; 黒 is the noun for the colour and needs い to modify a noun

ja: **実[じつ]**は俺[おれ]が魔王[まおう]だ
en: Actually I'm the demon lord; 実は prefaces a revelation the listener did not know — not an oath of honesty

ja: その**場所[ばしょ]**を知[し]っているか
en: Do you know that place?; 場所 is a physical spot you could point to; 所 is looser and can mean an aspect

ja: **上位[じょうい]**の魔物[まもの]だ
en: It's a higher-tier monster; 上位 ranks something above others in a hierarchy and labels evolved monster grades here

ja: **自由[じゆう]**になりたい
en: I want to be free; 自由 is "self" + "reason" — acting on your own will; it takes な before a noun

ja: そんな**存在[そんざい]**はいない
en: No such being exists; 存在 is both existence and the thing existing — often used for a presence too vast to name

ja: **村[むら]**のみんなを呼[よ]べ
en: Call everyone in the village; 村 is a small farming settlement while 町 is a town with shops

ja: この**地[ち]**は俺[おれ]の国[くに]だ
en: This land is my country; 地 means ground or territory and mostly lives in compounds; a plot you own is 土地[とち]

ja: この話[はなし]は**終[お]わった**
en: This conversation is over; 終わる is intransitive — things end on their own; ending something yourself is 終[お]える

ja: **結界[けっかい]**の中[なか]にいる
en: It's inside the barrier; 結界 is a bounded zone sealed by magic — the word comes from Buddhist consecrated ground

ja: **先[さき]**に行[い]ってくれ
en: Go on ahead; 先 is ahead in space or earlier in time; お先に excuses you for leaving before others

ja: **邪魔[じゃま]**をするな
en: Don't get in my way; 邪魔 is an obstruction; お邪魔します is what you say stepping into someone's home

ja: 一人[ひとり]では**無理[むり]**だ
en: Alone it's impossible; 無理 is "no reason" — forcing past what can be done; 無理するな warns against overdoing it

ja: あいつは俺[おれ]の**兄[あに]**だ
en: He's my older brother; 兄 is your own brother spoken of plainly; someone else's is お兄[にい]さん

ja: **ドワーフ**の作[つく]った剣[けん]だ
en: A dwarf-made sword; ドワーフ is the fantasy smith race — in the show they run the armed nation

ja: 竜[りゅう]を**封印[ふういん]**した
en: They sealed the dragon; 封印 is "seal" + "stamp" — locking something away by magic instead of killing it

ja: 今日[きょう]の**内[うち]**に戻[もど]る
en: I'll be back before the day is out; 〜のうちに means within that span; 内 also marks one's own side or group

ja: **解析[かいせき]**が終[お]わった
en: Analysis complete; 解析 is taking something apart to understand its workings; a simple appraisal is 鑑定[かんてい]

ja: 首領[しゅりょう]に**報告[ほうこく]**しろ
en: Report to the chief; 報告 is a formal account of results passed upward; casual news is 知[し]らせ

ja: お前[まえ]には**関係[かんけい]**ない
en: None of your business; 関係 is the link between things or people and 関係ない denies any involvement

ja: 俺[おれ]に**付[つ]いて**来[こ]い
en: Follow me; 付く is to be attached to something — 付いて来る is tagging along behind someone

ja: **我々[われわれ]**は仲間[なかま]だ
en: We are comrades; 我々 is formal and speech-making; among friends you'd say 俺たち

ja: この**戦[たたか]い**に勝[か]つ
en: We'll win this battle; 戦い is the noun from 戦う and covers a fight or campaign; a whole war is 戦争[せんそう]

ja: まだ**立[た]てる**か
en: Can you still stand?; 立つ is a person standing upright; a building standing is 建[た]つ

ja: 俺[おれ]は**すぐ**行[い]く
en: I'm going right away; すぐ is immediacy in either time or distance — すぐそこ means right over there — and it usually takes に before a verb in careful speech

ja: それは**意味[いみ]**が分[わ]からない
en: I don't get what that means; 意味 is the sense a word or an act carries; 意味がない is dismissing something as pointless rather than saying it lacks a dictionary definition

ja: お前[まえ]の**役[やく]**は何[なん]だ
en: What's your part in this; 役 is the role you play inside a group or a play; 役に立つ means to be useful. The concrete job itself is 仕事

ja: **勝手[かって]**な事[こと]を言[い]うな
en: Don't just say whatever you like; 勝手 decomposes as win plus hand and describes acting without consulting anyone. 勝手にしろ is an irritated do as you please

ja: **また**来[き]てくれ
en: Come again; また marks a repeat of the same event. Do not confuse it with まだ which means still or not yet — one vowel apart with opposite jobs

ja: オークの**討伐[とうばつ]**に行[い]く
en: We're going on the orc subjugation; 討伐 is attack plus cut down — a formal campaign authorised against a threat. It is quest and army vocabulary while 戦う is any fight

ja: **森林[しんりん]**の中[なか]に入[はい]る
en: We head into the woodland; 森林 is the Sino-Japanese forest plus woods used in place names and official talk like 大森林. In conversation people just say 森

ja: **狼[おおかみ]**が森[もり]から出[で]た
en: A wolf came out of the forest; the reading おおかみ is irregular and shifts to ろう in compounds. In the show these are the Direwolves that attack the goblin village

ja: **今後[こんご]**は気[き]を付[つ]けろ
en: Be careful from now on; 今後 is now plus after and always looks forward and is common in reports and pledges. 以後 can instead mean from that past point onward

ja: 名前[なまえ]を**教[おし]えて**くれ
en: Tell me your name; 教える covers plain telling as well as instructing so asking 教えて for a name is not requesting a lesson

ja: 準備[じゅんび]を**行[おこな]う**
en: We will carry out the preparations; 行う shares its kanji with 行く but means conduct or hold — ceremonies and operations. It never describes physically going anywhere

ja: 敵[てき]が**逃[に]げた**
en: The enemy fled; 逃げる is escaping danger and is intransitive — what you flee takes から. Letting something get away is 逃がす

ja: あの**女[おんな]**は強[つよ]い
en: That woman is strong; bare 女 is blunt and sounds dismissive when a character says あの女. Polite alternatives are 女の人 and 女性

ja: **確認[かくにん]**が必要[ひつよう]だ
en: We need to confirm it; 確認 is making sure plus recognising — verifying a fact or a state. It is not agreeing to something

ja: **ユニーク**スキルを得[え]た
en: I obtained a Unique Skill; here ユニーク is a fixed power tier of one-of-a-kind skills ranking above 上位 abilities. In everyday Japanese it just means quirky

ja: **なぜ**俺[おれ]を殺[ころ]す
en: Why are you killing me; なぜ is the formal written why and sounds declamatory aloud. どうして is the neutral spoken choice and なんで the casual one

ja: **牙[きば]**で敵[てき]を倒[たお]す
en: They bring down enemies with their fangs; 牙 is a predator's fang while 歯 is an ordinary tooth. The reading turns to が inside compounds

ja: **一緒[いっしょ]**に行[い]こう
en: Let's go together; 一緒 needs に to work adverbially. It also means identical — 一緒だ says two things are the same not that they are side by side

ja: オークは**豚[ぶた]**みたいだ
en: Orcs look like pigs; 豚 is the animal and doubles as an insult. This show leans on it — its orcs are the pig-headed race

ja: 勝[か]つのは**当然[とうぜん]**だ
en: Of course we win; 当然 asserts that something needed no saying. Used as a reply it carries a whiff of arrogance which is why villains reach for it

ja: この**料理[りょうり]**はうまい
en: This dish is delicious; 料理 is both the act of cooking and the finished dish. Food in general is 食べ物

ja: スキルを**獲得[かくとく]**した
en: Skill acquired; 獲得 is capture plus obtain and sounds like an announcement — the Sage voice uses it for gained abilities. People say 手に入れる instead

ja: その剣[けん]は**高[たか]い**
en: That sword is expensive; 高い covers height price and pitch alike. Its opposite is 低い for height but 安い for price

ja: 俺[おれ]は**負[ま]けない**
en: I won't lose; 負ける marks the winner with に as in 敵に負ける. It also means to give in to pressure or temptation

ja: **よし**やろう
en: All right let's do it; よし is a self-directed psych-up at the moment of deciding — grown from いい and addressed to nobody

ja: **失礼[しつれい]**な奴[やつ]だ
en: What a rude guy; the compound is lose plus courtesy. As a set phrase 失礼します is what you say entering or leaving a room

ja: **時間[じかん]**がない
en: There's no time; 時間 is measurable duration or a clock hour whereas 時 is the moment when something happens

ja: 体[からだ]が**回復[かいふく]**した
en: My body has recovered; 回復 is returning to a former state — health stamina or hit points. Healing magic uses it while 治る is the everyday get better

ja: **日[ひ]**が出[で]るまで待[ま]て
en: Wait until the sun comes up; 日 is both day and sun and its reading jumps around by compound — か in 三日 and にち in 日本

ja: 力[ちから]を**上[あ]げる**
en: I'm going to raise my power; 上げる is the transitive twin of 上がる. It also means to give upward to a superior and as a suffix 〜てあげる is doing a favour for someone

ja: 町[まち]に**向[む]かう**
en: We're heading for the town; 向かう stresses facing and aiming at a destination marked with に or へ unlike plain 行く. 〜に向かって is facing someone

ja: 我々[われわれ]の**目的[もくてき]**を言[い]おう
en: Let me state our purpose; 目的 is eye plus target — the aim behind an act. The measurable target you check progress against is 目標

ja: 俺[おれ]の**配下[はいか]**になれ
en: Become my retainer; 配下 is literally under one's arrangement and is what a demon lord calls sworn followers. 部下 is a mere workplace junior

ja: 戦[たたか]いを**始[はじ]める**
en: We begin the battle; 始める is transitive — you start a thing. 始まる is a thing starting by itself and as a suffix 〜始める means to start doing

ja: お前[まえ]は**神[かみ]**じゃない
en: You're no god; 神 is any of countless kami not a single creator. In this world it also names a power tier standing above demon lords

ja: **彼[かれ]**は勇者[ゆうしゃ]だ
en: He is the hero; in speech 彼 is usually replaced by a name or by あいつ. It also means boyfriend so scatter it carefully

ja: 姿[すがた]が**変[か]わった**
en: Its form changed; 変わる is intransitive — the thing changes on its own while 変える is you changing it. The homophone 帰る is going home

ja: これで**安心[あんしん]**だ
en: Now we can relax; 安心 is a peaceful heart — the state left once worry lifts. It is the opposite of 心配 and 安心しろ reassures someone

ja: **つまり**お前[まえ]が敵[てき]か
en: So you're the enemy then; つまり restates what was just said in plainer words and introduces your conclusion. だから supplies a cause instead

ja: **魂[たましい]**を食[く]った
en: It ate the soul; 魂 is the animating spirit that outlives the body while 心 is mind and heart. In this show souls are literally consumed and hoarded

ja: 名[な]を**与[あた]える**
en: I grant you a name; 与える is a superior bestowing something downward with に marking the recipient. Rimuru's naming of monsters uses exactly this verb not あげる

ja: **西方[せいほう]**から来[き]た
en: They came from the west; 西方 is the compass direction in formal geography. The show's 西方聖教会 is the Western Church whose lands sit west of the forest

ja: **別[べつ]**の所[ところ]へ行[い]く
en: I'm going somewhere else; 別 picks a different one of the same kind. 別に with a negative is a flat not particularly and works as a brush-off

ja: **全[まった]く**分[わ]からない
en: I have absolutely no idea; 全く intensifies and pairs with negatives for not at all. Standing alone it is an exasperated good grief

ja: **とても**強[つよ]い魔物[まもの]だ
en: It's a very strong monster; とても is the neutral intensifier and with a negative shifts to could not possibly. Casual speech prefers すごく

ja: それは**間違[まちが]い**だ
en: That's a mistake; a 間違い is an error of fact or judgement not a moral wrong. 間違いない does not mean flawless — it means there is no doubt

ja: 王国[おうこく]の**軍[ぐん]**が来[く]る
en: The kingdom's army is coming; 軍 is the fighting force as an institution and rarely stands alone in speech — expect 軍隊 or 大軍

ja: 嫌[いや]な**感[かん]じ**がする
en: I've got a bad feeling; 感じ is the impression a thing gives off from 感じる whereas 気持ち is your own inner state

ja: **聖教[せいきょう]**の騎士[きし]だ
en: He's a knight of the holy faith; 聖教 is holy plus teaching and in practice appears only inside the name 西方聖教会. Religion in general is 宗教

ja: **冒険[ぼうけん]**に出[で]る
en: I'm setting out on an adventure; 冒険 literally braves the danger and yields 冒険者 the guild-registered adventurer. It also covers any risky gamble

ja: **頭[あたま]**を使[つか]え
en: Use your head; 頭 is the physical head but also brains — 頭がいい means clever rather than a well-shaped skull

ja: **そちら**の話[はなし]を聞[き]きたい
en: I want to hear your side; そちら points to the listener's side and doubles as a polite you; そっち is the casual form

ja: **国家[こっか]**の敵[てき]だ
en: He is an enemy of the state; 国家 is the state as a political machine while 国 is the land and people you come from

ja: まだ**生[い]きて**いる
en: He is still alive; 生きる is living as an ongoing act — being alive is 生きている since there is no adjective for it

ja: **一体[いったい]**お前[まえ]は誰[だれ]だ
en: Just who the hell are you; 一体 loads a question word with pressure or disbelief; it is not the counter one body

ja: みんなの**おかげ**だ
en: It is thanks to everyone; おかげ credits someone for a good result; blame uses せい instead. Written お陰 it is the shelter of a shadow

ja: 一緒[いっしょ]に**遊[あそ]ぼう**
en: Let us hang out together; 遊ぶ is not childish — adults 遊ぶ too and it stretches to toying with an opponent

ja: 魔法[まほう]の**エネルギー**を得[え]た
en: I gained magical energy; エネルギー is fuel stored in a thing while 力 is strength someone exerts

ja: お前[まえ]に**感謝[かんしゃ]**する
en: I thank you from the heart; 感謝 is feel plus thanks and 感謝する is a formal declaration far heavier than ありがとう

ja: **ぜひ**来[き]てくれ
en: Do please come; ぜひ pushes an invitation or a wish and needs a request or desire after it — never a flat statement of fact

ja: 戦[たたか]いを**楽[たの]しむ**
en: I enjoy a good fight; 楽しむ is active — you go out and make the fun happen; 楽しい only labels something as fun

ja: あいつは**デーモン**だ
en: That guy is a demon; in this show デーモン names a specific higher demon race while 悪魔 is the loose word for any devil

ja: **さっき**の音[おと]は何[なん]だ
en: What was that sound just now; さっき is casual and vague — minutes ago at most; the formal version is 先ほど

ja: 俺[おれ]が**一番[いちばん]**強[つよ]い
en: I am the strongest; 一番 is literally number one and does the work of English -est since adjectives never inflate

ja: **どうぞ**食[た]べてください
en: Please help yourself; どうぞ hands something over or grants permission; asking for something instead needs お願い

ja: ここは**危険[きけん]**だ
en: It is dangerous here; 危険 states danger coolly and objectively while 危ない is what you shout as the rock falls

ja: それは**困[こま]る**
en: That puts me in a bind; 困る is the speaker being stuck or inconvenienced rather than an emotion; the thing itself is a 問題

ja: 強[つよ]い力[ちから]を**感[かん]じる**
en: I sense a strong power; 感じる is picking something up through the senses or gut; 思う is holding an opinion

ja: **今度[こんど]**は負[ま]けない
en: I will not lose this time; 今度 slides between this coming time and next time; 今回 pins it to this one instance

ja: 人間[にんげん]の**言葉[ことば]**が分[わ]かる
en: I understand human speech; 言葉 covers a word a phrase and a whole language; a dictionary item is a 単語

ja: **全員[ぜんいん]**逃[に]げろ
en: Everyone run; 全員 counts every member of a defined group and sounds like an order; みんな is warm and vague

ja: 後[あと]何[なん]**分[ぷん]**だ
en: How many minutes left; 分 is the minute counter and flips between ふん and ぷん depending on the number before it

ja: **そいつ**は敵[てき]か
en: Is that guy an enemy; そいつ is rough for someone the listener knows of and is an insult said to their face

ja: **新[あたら]しい**名前[なまえ]をくれ
en: Give me a new name; 新しい also means fresh or current; a newly arrived person is a 新人 — 新しい人 sounds like a replacement

ja: **妹[いもうと]**を守[まも]る
en: I will protect my little sister; 妹 is only your own younger sister; someone else's is 妹さん and no word covers sister without age

ja: **いろいろ**な物[もの]がある
en: There are all sorts of things; いろいろ spreads across kinds and is 色々 in kanji — the color glyph doubled

ja: 魔物[まもの]を**捕食[ほしょく]**した
en: I devoured the monster; 捕食 is catch plus eat — a predator taking prey and the name of Rimuru's Predator skill

ja: 俺[おれ]は**本気[ほんき]**だ
en: I am serious; 本気 is true spirit — you are not joking or holding back; 本気を出す is dropping the limiter and going all out

ja: **予定[よてい]**が変[か]わった
en: The plan has changed; 予定 is pre plus decide — an arrangement already on the calendar; つもり is a private intention

ja: その**程度[ていど]**か
en: Is that all you have got; 程度 measures how far something reaches and その程度 waves an amount away as beneath notice

ja: **面倒[めんどう]**な事[こと]になった
en: This has turned into a hassle; 面倒 is trouble that costs you effort; 面倒を見る flips it into looking after someone

ja: これは**まずい**
en: This is bad; まずい is bad-tasting food and equally the noise you make when a plan is falling apart. Its opposite both ways is うまい

ja: これで**最後[さいご]**だ
en: This is the last one; 最後 is most plus after — final in a sequence. Its homophone 最期 means a person's dying moment

ja: **巣[す]**に戻[もど]る
en: It is heading back to the nest; 巣 stretches over nests hives and dens — any creature's base including a monster lair or a gang hideout

ja: 中[なか]に**入[い]れて**くれ
en: Let me put it inside; 入れる is the transitive twin of 入る — you place something in rather than going in yourself

ja: **陛下[へいか]**が待[ま]っている
en: His Majesty is waiting; 陛下 hangs after a monarch's title as Majesty and is never used of yourself

ja: その**格好[かっこう]**は何[なん]だ
en: What is that getup; 格好 is your outward look and outfit; squeezed to かっこいい it becomes the everyday word for cool

ja: **絶対[ぜったい]**に許[ゆる]さない
en: I will never forgive that; 絶対 pushes to definitely with a positive verb and to never with a negative one

ja: 俺[おれ]も**連[つ]れて**行[い]け
en: Take me along too; 連れる brings a person with you and almost always rides on 行く or 来る; objects go by 持って行く

ja: ここに**残[のこ]る**
en: I am staying here; 残る is something being left over by itself while 残す is deliberately leaving it behind

ja: **姉[あね]**に頼[たの]む
en: I will ask my big sister; 姉 is your own older sister in plain form; you call her お姉ちゃん and hers is お姉さん

ja: 名[な]を**忘[わす]れた**
en: I forgot the name; 忘れる is both losing a fact and leaving an object behind and it takes を where English adds about

ja: その**顔[かお]**を見[み]せろ
en: Show me that face; 顔 is the face and by extension your standing — 顔を出す is turning up somewhere

ja: 我々[われわれ]に**対[たい]する**攻撃[こうげき]だ
en: It is an attack aimed at us; 対する marks the target something points at and 〜に対して also frames an attitude toward someone

ja: **種族[しゅぞく]**が違[ちが]う
en: We are different races; 種族 is a race as a people — orcs elves dwarves; bare biology is 種

ja: **戦争[せんそう]**をやめろ
en: Stop this war; 戦争 is full nation-scale war; one clash is a 戦い and a campaign to wipe out a threat is 討伐

ja: 今日[きょう]は**楽[たの]しい**
en: Today is fun; 楽しい reports that the speaker is having a good time so it describes occasions more readily than people

ja: **おいしい**物[もの]を食[た]べたい
en: I want to eat something delicious; おいしい is the neutral polite praise while うまい is blunt and masculine and can also mean skilled

ja: **上[うえ]**を見[み]ろ
en: Look up; 上 is above or on top and also higher standing; for a rank tier proper the word is 上位

ja: 頭[あたま]の中[なか]の声[こえ]が**解[かい]**と言[い]った
en: The voice in my head said understood; 解 is a bare answer or solution and the Great Sage clips it into a confirmation like affirmative

ja: この**洞窟[どうくつ]**の中[なか]は危険[きけん]だ
en: It's dangerous inside this cave; 洞窟 is a natural hole in rock — the word says nothing about monsters or floors; a built maze needs 迷宮 instead

ja: **まじ**で言[い]ってるのか
en: Are you serious?; clipped slang from 真面目 and used adverbially as まじで; far too casual to aim at anyone you owe respect

ja: 俺[おれ]を**なめる**な
en: Don't underestimate me; the verb is literally to lick; taking someone lightly is pictured as licking them and なめるな is a fighting word

ja: **期待[きたい]**してもいいか
en: Can I get my hopes up?; 期待 is hoping for good things from someone else's performance so it carries pressure; 予定 is a scheduled plan with no hope in it

ja: これからも**よろしく**
en: Let's keep getting along; literally asks to be treated favourably — it covers hello nice to meet you and please handle this for me depending on the situation

ja: なんて**素晴[すば]らしい**世界[せかい]だ
en: What a wonderful world; 素晴らしい is admiring the quality of something and fits a speech; 凄い is the casual all-purpose burst of awe

ja: その**件[けん]**は聞[き]いている
en: I've heard about that matter; 件 is the businesslike counter for incidents and items of business; the show's title uses 〜した件 like a case-file heading

ja: その**理由[りゆう]**を教[おし]えてくれ
en: Tell me the reason; 理由 is the reason you can state out loud while 訳 is the underlying circumstances and mostly shows up glued into grammar

ja: それは**大変[たいへん]**だったな
en: That must have been rough; as an adjective it means dire but stuck in front of another word it only intensifies — 大変助かる is a huge help

ja: **無事[ぶじ]**で良[よ]かった
en: I'm glad you're safe; decomposes into no incident so it means you came through danger unhurt; a place being free of hazards is 安全

ja: お前[まえ]の**気持[きも]ち**は分[わ]かる
en: I know how you feel; 気持ち is the emotion or bodily sensation felt from inside; 感じ is the impression a thing gives off to you

ja: 俺[おれ]も**参加[さんか]**するぞ
en: I'm joining in too; 参加 is adding yourself to an event or effort that already exists; it never means joining an organisation permanently

ja: **ダンジョン**を作[つく]る
en: We're building a dungeon; a game loanword for a floored monster lair you clear; used interchangeably with 迷宮 in the show's dialogue

ja: **成功[せいこう]**したぞ
en: It worked!; 成功 is the achieved outcome of a deliberate attempt so it needs a plan behind it; a lucky break would be 運

ja: お前[まえ]は俺[おれ]の**下[した]**だ
en: You rank below me; 下 is under in space and under in hierarchy; read した standing alone but か or げ inside compounds like 配下

ja: **魔力[まりょく]**を使[つか]い過[す]ぎた
en: I used too much magic power; 魔力 is the fuel you spend while 魔法 is the spell you spend it on

ja: お前[まえ]がいて**助[たす]かった**
en: Having you here saved me; the intransitive twin of 助ける so the rescued one is the subject; on its own it is the everyday that's a big help

ja: **怒[おこ]らないで**くれ
en: Don't get mad; 怒る is anger flaring into view rather than a mood held quietly; 怒られる shifts to being scolded by someone

ja: 敵[てき]は**既[すで]に**死[し]んでいる
en: The enemy is already dead; 既に is the written and dramatic register of もう and only reports facts — it cannot mean any more in a negative

ja: お前[まえ]は少[すこ]し**黙[だま]れ**
en: You be quiet for a while; 黙る is the act of going silent not the state of being silent; the bare imperative 黙れ is aggressive

ja: **せっかく**作[つく]った料理[りょうり]だぞ
en: I went to all that trouble cooking this; せっかく flags effort or a rare chance that risks going to waste and colours the whole sentence

ja: 俺[おれ]たちは**友達[ともだち]**だろ
en: We're friends aren't we?; 友達 is a personal friend chosen freely; 仲間 is someone inside your group whether you like them or not

ja: その力[ちから]を**利用[りよう]**する
en: We'll put that power to use; 利用 is turning something to your advantage and sounds calculating about people; 使う is plain handling

ja: それで**よろしい**
en: That will do; the stiff formal 良い used to grant approval downward; a subordinate answering upward says 結構です rather than this

ja: **普通[ふつう]**の人間[にんげん]じゃない
en: He's no ordinary human; 普通 is the unremarkable baseline and works as a noun so it takes の before another noun

ja: もっと**話[はな]そう**
en: Let's talk more; 話す is the act of speaking with someone while 言う points at the words uttered and 聞く at the ear

ja: **完全[かんぜん]**に負[ま]けた
en: I lost utterly; 完全 says nothing is missing so 完全に works as an adverb meaning through and through; 絶対 is about certainty instead

ja: **能力[のうりょく]**を得[え]た
en: I gained an ability; 能力 is general capacity you possess; a スキル is one named power granted by this world's system

ja: **さっさと**行[い]け
en: Get a move on; さっさと is impatient — hurry up and finish — while 早く merely asks for speed and can be gentle

ja: **まず**話[はなし]を聞[き]け
en: Hear me out first; まず orders steps in an argument or plan and often pairs with a later 次に; it is not the earliest point in time

ja: これは**命令[めいれい]**だ
en: This is an order; 命令 comes down from authority and refusing it is disobedience; 頼む asks a favour between equals

ja: その**場合[ばあい]**はどうする
en: What do we do in that case?; 場合 is a hypothetical set of circumstances despite the 場 kanji — never a physical spot

ja: **最初[さいしょ]**から知[し]っていた
en: I knew from the very start; 最初 is the first item in a sequence and mirrors 最後; まず is first as a step to take

ja: **師匠[ししょう]**と呼[よ]んでくれ
en: Call me master; 師匠 is the master of a craft you apprentice under and the pupil is a 弟子; 主 is a master you serve

ja: **迷宮[めいきゅう]**の下[した]に行[い]く
en: We're going down into the labyrinth; 迷宮 is lost plus palace — the classical maze that confuses you; the show says ダンジョン for the same building

ja: **たった**一人[ひとり]で戦[たたか]った
en: He fought all on his own; たった clings to a number to stress how tiny it is and needs that number present

ja: お前[まえ]の**行動[こうどう]**は早[はや]かった
en: You acted fast; 行動 is observable conduct or a course of action taken by a person; 動き is bare physical motion

ja: 時間[じかん]が**かかる**な
en: This is going to take a while; the cost or time is the subject here and かける is the transitive partner you apply to something

ja: お前[まえ]から**名乗[なの]れ**
en: You give your name first; 名乗る is declaring your own name or title and can mean claiming one you have no right to

ja: この**場[ば]**は俺[おれ]に任[まか]せろ
en: Leave this situation to me; 場 is the occasion or scene unfolding rather than a location on a map — that is 場所

ja: **理解[りかい]**できない
en: I can't make sense of it; 理解 is grasping how something works and stays formal and mental; 分かる is the everyday spoken verb

ja: これが**結果[けっか]**だ
en: This is the result; 結果 is what a cause produced and often ends a sentence as a verdict; 効果 is the effect worked on a target

ja: 私[わたし]の**生徒[せいと]**だった
en: They were my pupils; 生徒 is a school pupil paired with 先生; the follower of a 師匠 is a 弟子 instead

ja: **効果[こうか]**がない
en: It has no effect; 効果 is the impact something produces where it lands so poison and medicine both have it; the outcome itself is 結果

ja: 強[つよ]い**個体[こたい]**が残[のこ]る
en: The strong individuals survive; 個体 is the biology term for one organism counted apart from its species — 一人 will not do for a monster

ja: 森[もり]を**調査[ちょうさ]**する
en: We'll survey the forest; 調査 is organised fact-finding over time; 確認 is a quick check and 解析 is picking data apart

ja: 敵[てき]の**動[うご]き**が見[み]える
en: I can see the enemy's movements; the noun off 動く covers physical motion and also troop or market trends; 行動 adds intent

ja: **ボス**は下[した]にいる
en: The boss is down below; a loanword for the top monster of a lair or the head of a gang; in-world ranks use 首領 or 主

ja: **見事[みごと]**な戦[たたか]いだった
en: That was a splendid fight; 見事 is literally worth seeing and praises skilled execution from a spectator's seat

ja: **命[いのち]**だけは助[たす]けてくれ
en: Just spare my life; 命 is the single life you can lose and it appears in oaths; the act of living is 生きる

ja: 俺[おれ]の**実力[じつりょく]**を見[み]せてやる
en: I'll show you what I can really do; 実力 is real plus power — capability actually demonstrated as opposed to rank or reputation

ja: 魔法[まほう]で**操[あやつ]られた**
en: He was being controlled by magic; 操る is pulling strings from outside — a puppet a machine or someone's mind; 使う is merely putting a tool to use

ja: **新[あら]たな**仲間[なかま]が来[き]た
en: A new comrade has arrived; 新た is the stiff written twin of 新しい and behaves as a na-adjective — 新たな仲間 never 新たい

ja: 今日[きょう]から**訓練[くんれん]**を始[はじ]める
en: Training starts today; 訓練 is drilling to a program — 練習 is casual repetition and 修行 is ascetic discipline

ja: その**店[みせ]**で待[ま]っている
en: I'll be waiting at that shop; 店 names the premises — a stall a bar or a restaurant all count and it takes に for going and で for buying

ja: **そろそろ**帰[かえ]るか
en: About time we headed back; そろそろ says the moment to act has quietly arrived — もうすぐ only predicts that something is near

ja: **口[くち]**が悪[わる]いな
en: You've got a foul mouth; 口 stretches from the body part to speech itself — and a bottle's opening or a cave mouth take the same word

ja: **ちゃんと**仕事[しごと]をしろ
en: Do the job properly; ちゃんと is casual spoken the way it ought to be done — きちんと is its tidier written cousin

ja: あいつは強[つよ]い**戦士[せんし]**だ
en: That guy is a strong warrior; 戦士 is the fighter role itself — 騎士 implies sworn service to a lord and 兵士 a soldier in someone's army

ja: では**参[まい]ります**
en: Well then — I'm on my way; 参る is the humble verb for both going and coming used toward a superior; shouted in a fight it means here I come

ja: **大[おお]きい**魔物[まもの]が出[で]た
en: A big monster showed up; 大きい measures physical size while 多い means numerous — before a noun the written form is 大きな

ja: 次回[じかい]が**楽[たの]しみ**だ
en: I'm looking forward to the next one; 楽しみ is the noun of anticipation so the pleasure is still ahead; 楽しい describes fun happening now

ja: みんな**元気[げんき]**か
en: Is everyone doing all right; 元気 is origin plus spirit — it covers both sound health and visible liveliness

ja: 会[あ]えて**嬉[うれ]しい**
en: I'm glad we could meet; 嬉しい is the spike of gladness at an event while 幸[しあわ]せ is lasting contentment — and it reports your own feeling so it sits oddly on a third person

ja: **説明[せつめい]**してくれ
en: Explain it to me; 説明 lays out how something works for someone who does not know — excusing yourself is 言い訳 and a briefing upward is 報告

ja: 新[あら]たな力[ちから]が**生[う]まれた**
en: A new power was born; 生まれる is intransitive — the thing comes into being by itself; 生[う]む is somebody producing it

ja: 何[なに]も**恐[おそ]れない**
en: I fear nothing; 恐れる is the deliberate verb of dreading a thing — 怖[こわ]い is the adjective for how frightened you feel at this moment

ja: その**技[わざ]**は見[み]えなかった
en: I couldn't even see that move; 技 is a honed physical move such as a named finisher — a system power you possess is スキル

ja: **状況[じょうきょう]**を報告[ほうこく]しろ
en: Report the situation; 状況 is how circumstances stand right now so it shifts minute to minute — 状態 is the fixed condition of one thing

ja: 命令[めいれい]に**従[したが]え**
en: Obey the order; 従う takes に and means falling in behind someone's lead — walking along after a person is ついていく

ja: 俺[おれ]も**同[おな]じ**気持[きも]ちだ
en: I feel the same way; 同じ is the odd na-adjective that drops な before a noun — 同じ人 never 同じな人

ja: 時間[じかん]が**足[た]りない**
en: There isn't enough time; 足りる is intransitive and marks the thing with が — the amount suffices by itself so you cannot 足りる something

ja: **しっかり**持[も]ってろ
en: Hold on tight; しっかり stresses firmness and reliability — of a grip or of a person's character; ちゃんと only says the job met the standard

ja: 仲間[なかま]を**紹介[しょうかい]**する
en: Let me introduce my companions; 紹介 is presenting one party to another — stating your own name instead is 名乗る

ja: **冗談[じょうだん]**だろ
en: You have to be joking; 冗談 is a remark not meant seriously — and 冗談じゃない protests that a situation is unacceptable rather than unfunny

ja: あの魔物[まもの]は**やばい**
en: That monster is seriously bad news; やばい began as thieves' slang for dangerous and younger speakers now use it for anything extreme including great — tone decides which

ja: 一緒[いっしょ]に**飲[の]もう**
en: Let's have a drink; 飲む covers taking anything down unchewed — soup medicine and pills; on its own it usually implies alcohol

ja: **計画[けいかく]**は簡単[かんたん]だ
en: The plan is simple; 計画 is a worked-out scheme with steps — 予定 is only what is scheduled and つもり a private intention

ja: それは**罠[わな]**だ
en: That's a trap; 罠 is a snare deliberately set — you fall into one with 罠にはまる and it works for verbal traps too

ja: お前[まえ]は**甘[あま]い**な
en: You're too soft; 甘い runs from sweet taste to going easy on people to naive optimism — calling a judgement 甘い says it underrates the danger

ja: 村[むら]の**住民[じゅうみん]**を守[まも]る
en: I'll protect the people of the village; 住民 is dwell plus people — whoever lives in a given place; it is flat administrative wording

ja: **初[はじ]めて**人間[にんげん]を見[み]た
en: I saw a human for the first time; 初めて marks a first-ever experience while 最初 only labels which item comes first in a sequence

ja: **失敗[しっぱい]**は許[ゆる]さない
en: Failure will not be forgiven; 失敗 is a botched attempt measured against your own aim — losing to an opponent is 負ける

ja: いいぞ **ただし**俺[おれ]も行[い]く
en: Fine but I'm coming too; ただし attaches a restricting proviso to what was just granted while しかし merely contrasts

ja: **ドラゴン**が来[く]るぞ
en: The dragon is coming; ドラゴン is the western beast and 竜 the same creature in Sino-Japanese dress — the show uses the loanword for the species itself

ja: 約束[やくそく]を**結[むす]ぶ**
en: We'll seal the promise; 結ぶ literally knots a cord so pacts and alliances are tied — rounding off a speech is also 結ぶ

ja: 俺[おれ]を**騙[だま]した**のか
en: Did you trick me; 騙す requires intent by the deceiver — an honest slip is 間違い and 嘘をつく is only the act of telling the lie

ja: **なかなか**強[つよ]いな
en: Pretty strong; なかなか before a positive means impressively so — paired with a negative it flips to not easily at all

ja: 剣[けん]が**要[い]る**
en: I need a sword; 要る marks the needed thing with が and is godan so the negative is 要らない — 必要 is its noun-shaped twin

ja: **腕[うで]**を上[あ]げたな
en: Your skill has improved; 腕 is the arm from shoulder to wrist and by metaphor hands-on ability — 腕がいい praises craft not muscle

ja: 俺[おれ]の**真似[まね]**をするな
en: Quit copying me; 真似 is mimicking someone's manner and usually carries a scolding — 真似をする also covers pulling a foolish stunt

ja: 敵[てき]の**軍勢[ぐんぜい]**が見[み]える
en: I can see the enemy host; 軍勢 counts an army as a visible mass of troops on the march — 軍 is the organization and 兵 the single soldier

ja: **交渉[こうしょう]**は俺[おれ]がやる
en: I'll handle the negotiations; 交渉 is bargaining where both sides give ground — 話し合い is just talking it over and 相談 is seeking advice

ja: 私[わたし]はスライムと**申[もう]します**
en: My name is Slime; 申す is the humble verb for one's own speaking toward a superior and と申します is the formal way to give your name

ja: その話[はなし]に**興味[きょうみ]**がある
en: That story interests me; 興味 takes が ある with に on the target — 面白い describes the thing while 興味 is the pull you feel toward it

ja: 魔力[まりょく]が**増[ま]した**
en: My magic power has grown; 増す is a literary intransitive rise in amount or degree — 増[ふ]える is the everyday word and 増[ふ]やす is adding on purpose

ja: **水[みず]**を飲[の]む
en: I'm going to drink some water; 水 means cold water only — heated water has its own word お湯[ゆ] so asking for 水 gets you the plain cold stuff

ja: **マスター**の言[い]う通[とお]りだ
en: Just as you say Master; マスター is either the man behind a bar counter or someone who has mastered a craft — here it is how a bound spirit addresses its owner

ja: **思念[しねん]**で話[はな]せ
en: Talk to me by thought; 思念 is a thought pushed mind to mind and the show uses it for telepathic speech — plain thinking is 考える

ja: そいつの顔[かお]を**打[う]った**
en: I smacked him in the face; 打つ is one sharp blow with something held — 叩[たた]く is casual knocking and 手を打つ means taking measures

ja: 誰[だれ]も**答[こた]えない**
en: Nobody answers; 答える is replying to a question or a call — it takes に for the thing answered (質問に答える) not を

ja: 私[わたし]を**頼[たよ]って**ください
en: Please rely on me; 頼る is leaning on someone as support; 頼む is asking for one specific favour

ja: **油断[ゆだん]**するな
en: Don't drop your guard; literally oil + cutting off — the lamp goes out while you slack off; used for the fatal overconfidence right before a fight turns

ja: 魔力[まりょく]の**量[りょう]**が凄[すご]い
en: The amount of magical energy is insane; 量 counts uncountable bulk; use 数 for countable things

ja: お前[まえ]を**信用[しんよう]**していない
en: I don't trust you; 信用 is earned credit based on track record while 信じる is an act of faith right now

ja: 国[くに]を**滅[ほろ]ぼす**つもりか
en: Do you intend to destroy a nation; 滅ぼす wipes out a whole people or country — for smashing an object use 壊す

ja: 俺[おれ]が**決[き]める**
en: I'm the one who decides; 決める is transitive — the intransitive 決まる means a matter settles by itself

ja: ドワーフの**里[さと]**に行[い]く
en: I'm going to the dwarves' settlement; 里 is a homeland village with warm nostalgia attached; 村 is the neutral administrative word

ja: 人間[にんげん]と**同盟[どうめい]**を結[むす]ぶ
en: We form an alliance with the humans; 同盟 is a formal sworn pact between powers; 仲間 is just being on the same side

ja: 同盟[どうめい]の**盟主[めいしゅ]**になる
en: He becomes leader of the alliance; 盟主 is the chairing power of a pact — not a king; the 盟 is the blood oath itself

ja: **うるさい**な 黙[だま]れ
en: Shut it; うるさい starts as physically noisy but as a bark it means you are being annoying — also used for someone fussy about details

ja: 俺[おれ]は**構[かま]わない**
en: I don't mind; 構う is caring enough to be bothered; the negative is the standard way to grant permission

ja: 魔物[まもの]の**気配[けはい]**がする
en: I sense something out there; 気配 is a presence felt without seeing or hearing it — always paired with がする

ja: 凄[すご]い**オーラ**を感[かん]じる
en: I feel a tremendous aura; オーラ in the show is visible pressure radiating off strong beings; 気配 is far subtler

ja: ドワーフの**親父[おやじ]**は強[つよ]い
en: That dwarf geezer is tough; 親父 is my dad in rough male speech but for a stranger it's a familiar hey pops — rude to say to his face

ja: **死[し]**を恐[おそ]れるな
en: Do not fear death; 死 is the abstract noun and stays in written or grand speech; ordinary talk uses the verb 死ぬ

ja: 魔王[まおう]に**仕[つか]えている**
en: I serve the demon lord; 仕える is being in a lord's service permanently; 使う and 仕える share no meaning despite the sound

ja: あの**じじい**は何[なに]者[もの]だ
en: Who the hell is that old geezer; じじい stretches 爺 the kanji for an old man into a deliberate insult — pick 親父 or ご老人 if you don't want a fight

ja: 同[おな]じ**クラス**の生徒[せいと]だった
en: We were in the same class; クラス covers a school class and also a rank tier — the show uses it for monster grades

ja: **貴族[きぞく]**の格好[かっこう]だな
en: You're dressed like a noble; 貴族 is hereditary aristocracy; 王 is the crown itself

ja: 町[まち]で**祭[まつ]り**をやる
en: We'll hold a festival in town; 祭り is a public shrine-rooted celebration with stalls and crowds

ja: **宴[うたげ]**の用意[ようい]をしろ
en: Get the banquet ready; 宴 is the archaic literary word for a feast — nobles and demon lords say it; everyday speech says 宴会

ja: 名前[なまえ]を**覚[おぼ]えて**おけ
en: Remember my name; 覚える is getting it into your head; 思い出す is dragging it back out later

ja: **どんな**スキルだ
en: What kind of skill is it; どんな asks for a description and must sit in front of a noun; どう modifies verbs

ja: **どれ**がいい
en: Which one do you want; どれ picks from three or more with no noun after it; どの needs a noun

ja: 俺[おれ]の**せい**じゃない
en: It's not my fault; せい assigns blame for a bad outcome — for a good one use おかげ

ja: **戦力[せんりょく]**はこっちが上[うえ]だ
en: We've got the stronger force; 戦力 is a measurable combat asset counted in troops; 力 is raw strength

ja: 力[ちから]を**尽[つ]くす**
en: I'll do everything I can; 尽くす is using something up to zero — 全力を尽くす and 手を尽くす are the set phrases

ja: この森[もり]に**住[す]んでいる**
en: I live in this forest; 住む needs に for the place and is almost always in the ている form; 生きる is being alive not residing

ja: **仮面[かめん]**を取[と]れ
en: Take off the mask; 仮面 is literally temporary + face and carries the sense of a hidden true self

ja: ここは**安全[あんぜん]**だ
en: It's safe here; 安全 is objective absence of danger while 安心 is the relief you personally feel

ja: みんなに**伝[つた]えて**くれ
en: Pass it on to everyone; 伝える hands a message onward to a third party; 言う is just saying it

ja: **身[み]**を守[まも]れ
en: Protect yourself; 身 is your own person and body as one — 身を守る 身につける are set phrases where 体 won't work

ja: 誰[だれ]も**気付[きづ]かなかった**
en: Nobody noticed; 気付く is the moment awareness lands and takes に; 分かる is understanding the content

ja: 訓練[くんれん]を**続[つづ]けろ**
en: Keep up the training; 続ける is you continuing something; 続く is a thing carrying on by itself

ja: お前[まえ]なんか**怖[こわ]くない**
en: I'm not scared of you; 怖い describes the speaker's fear and also the frightening thing — context decides which

ja: 剣[けん]で**切[き]る**
en: I'll cut it with a sword; 切る is a clean blade stroke; it also hides in 電話を切る for hanging up

ja: **久[ひさ]しく**会[あ]っていないな
en: It's been ages since we last met; 久しい means much time has passed and its plain form is rare — you meet it almost only in the adverb 久しく and in 久しぶり

ja: 敵[てき]が**多[おお]い**
en: There are too many enemies; 多い cannot sit in front of a noun — say 敵が多い not 多い敵

ja: そんなに**弱[よわ]く**ないぞ
en: I'm not that weak; 弱い also covers being bad at something and drink or heat being weak

ja: **怪我[けが]**はないか
en: You're not hurt are you; 怪我 is external damage from an accident or fight; 病気 is illness

ja: 我[わ]が**意思[いし]**は変[か]わらない
en: My will is unchanged; 意思 is your intent to act while 意志 with 志 is willpower — 意味 looks close but is meaning

ja: **大臣[だいじん]**に報告[ほうこく]する
en: I'll report to the minister; 大臣 is literally great + retainer and denotes a crown appointment

ja: 結界[けっかい]が**完成[かんせい]**した
en: The barrier is complete; 完成 is a built thing reaching finished form; 終わる is any activity merely ending

ja: 子供[こども]の**世話[せわ]**を頼[たの]む
en: Look after the kid for me; 世話 is hands-on caretaking — お世話になりました thanks someone for having supported you

ja: 問題[もんだい]**なし**だ
en: No problems; なし is the blunt noun form of ない used on signs labels and clipped reports

ja: この国[くに]を**救[すく]う**
en: I'll save this country; 救う rescues from ruin or doom on a grand scale while 助ける can be a hand up with anything

ja: 何[なに]が**起[お]きた**
en: What happened; 起きる is both getting out of bed and an event occurring; 起こす is causing it

ja: **作戦[さくせん]**を説明[せつめい]する
en: I'll explain the plan; 作戦 is a battle plan with tactics; 計画 is any scheduled plan

ja: **マスク**を付[つ]けろ
en: Put your mask on; マスク is a worn face covering like a surgical mask; 仮面 is the rigid disguise kind

ja: **彼女[かのじょ]**は強[つよ]い人[ひと]だ
en: She is a strong person; 彼女 is 彼 plus 女 and doubles as girlfriend depending on context — Japanese normally drops such pronouns and uses a name instead

ja: この子[こ]は**かわいい**な
en: This kid is cute; covers small-and-endearing including pity for a helpless thing — 美しい is cold formal beauty and never used this way

ja: **東[ひがし]**の国[くに]へ行[い]く
en: We head for the eastern country; standalone it is ひがし but inside compounds it flips to とう as in 東方 — direction words take の before a noun

ja: 敵[てき]を**警戒[けいかい]**しろ
en: Stay on guard against the enemy; 警 warn plus 戒 guard — an ongoing watchful state you hold not a single action; 心配 is inner worry with no readiness

ja: **覚悟[かくご]**はできている
en: I am prepared; bracing yourself for the worst outcome rather than mere planning — 覚悟しろ is a threat meaning prepare to die

ja: 俺[おれ]が**責任[せきにん]**を取[と]る
en: I will take responsibility; accountability for a result after the fact so it pairs with 取る — the duties themselves are 仕事

ja: それは**残念[ざんねん]**だったな
en: That is a shame; disappointment that things turned out badly not personal sadness; 残念ながら softens bad news

ja: **炎[ほのお]**の魔法[まほう]を使[つか]う
en: I use fire magic; 炎 is a visible leaping blaze while 火 is fire as a thing or a flame source — compounds read えん

ja: 仲間[なかま]が**少[すく]ない**
en: We have few allies; an i-adjective about quantity being small so never about physical size which is 小さい; it prefers the predicate slot over sitting before a noun

ja: お前[まえ]を**受[う]け入[い]れる**
en: I will accept you; literally receive and put inside — taking a person or condition into your side; plain 受ける is only to receive or undergo

ja: 炎[ほのお]への**耐性[たいせい]**を獲得[かくとく]した
en: I gained resistance to fire; 耐 endure plus 性 nature — a standing immunity listed on your status screen not the act of putting up with something

ja: **ずっと**待[ま]っていた
en: I was waiting the whole time; unbroken continuation over a long stretch and also an intensifier in comparisons as in ずっと強い

ja: 敵[てき]の**数[かず]**が多[おお]い
en: The enemies are many; the count of things — a written numeral is 数字 and the compound reading is すう

ja: **どちら**が強[つよ]いですか
en: Which one is stronger; the polite form of どっち and it also asks a direction or even a person politely

ja: それが**ルール**だ
en: That is the rule; loanword for game and social rules where 規則 sounds bureaucratic and 命令 is a direct order

ja: 今回[こんかい]は俺[おれ]の**勝[か]ち**だ
en: This one is my win; the plain noun made from 勝つ used in scores and matches while 勝利 is grand narration

ja: お前[まえ]は何[なに]を**望[のぞ]む**
en: What do you wish for; desiring an outcome in a weighty distant way — 欲しい is everyday wanting and 願う is closer to praying

ja: 次[つぎ]の**階層[かいそう]**へ行[い]こう
en: Let us go to the next floor; 階 floor plus 層 layer so it names a labyrinth stratum — a plain building floor is just 階

ja: 一人[ひとり]**対[たい]**軍勢[ぐんぜい]か
en: One man against an army; read たい when placed between two opposing sides like a match card; the verb form is 対する

ja: この**草[くさ]**は料理[りょうり]に使[つか]う
en: We use this plant in cooking; it means herbs and wild plants generally not just lawn grass; the medicinal kind is 薬草

ja: **そもそも**お前[まえ]は誰[だれ]だ
en: Who even are you to begin with; it rewinds to the premise and usually hints the whole thing was wrong from the start

ja: スキルが**発動[はつどう]**した
en: The skill activated; 発 emit plus 動 move so the skill is the subject with が — 使う frames the same event as the user acting

ja: そんな**ひどい**事[こと]を言[い]うな
en: Do not say such cruel things; it spans morally cruel and merely severe so of weather or a wound it just means bad in degree

ja: 彼[かれ]は**元[もと]**騎士[きし]だ
en: He is a former knight; stuck in front of a noun it works like ex- while on its own it is the original state as in 元に戻る

ja: 俺[おれ]の**願[ねが]い**を聞[き]いてくれ
en: Hear my request; the noun of 願う covering both a plea aimed at someone and a prayer — お願い is the everyday please

ja: 誰[だれ]を**狙[ねら]って**いる
en: Who are you targeting; lining up a weapon or fixing on a person or prize — the prize itself is 目的

ja: 魔力[まりょく]の**影響[えいきょう]**だな
en: It is the effect of the magic power; 影 shadow plus 響 echo — a knock-on consequence that is neutral rather than 力 which is raw power

ja: これが**父[ちち]**の剣[けん]だ
en: This is my father's sword; 父 is how you name your own father to outsiders — you call him お父さん to his face and someone else's is also お父さん

ja: **遠慮[えんりょ]**しないで食[た]べて
en: Help yourself and eat; 遠 distant plus 慮 consideration — hanging back so as not to impose; 遠慮なく means go right ahead
